provenance: Hand-written list for the Topic Desk (assets/js/page/topic-desk-model.js). Drafted by Claude on 2026-10-19 for Ian's review. Every other sentence on the desk is computed from the library's data. A dek states what a topic covers and asks the question the churches answer. It never states an answer, a tradition's position, or Mere Orthodoxy's position. A fault-line row is shown only when every quotation in it is found, word for word, in the article the library maps to the topic. A verse note is a plain textual fact.

verseNotes.i-john.5.7: The wording of this verse that names the Father, the Word, and the Spirit is found in late Latin manuscripts and in a few late Greek manuscripts. It is absent from the critical Greek text. The text shown is the Verse Desk's default.

de-scriptura.dek: What the churches have said about the Bible. Its authority, sufficiency, and interpretation.

de-deo.dek: What the churches have taught about who God is and what God is like.

de-praedestinatione.dek: What the churches have said about election and predestination in relation to salvation.

de-creatione.dek: What the churches have said about the origin of the world and God's relation to it.

de-providentia.dek: What the churches have said about God's relation to the course of events.

de-peccato.dek: What the churches have taught about sin. Its origin and its effects.

de-christo.dek: The person and work of Jesus Christ. How the creeds, councils, and teachers describe them.

de-spiritu-sancto.dek: The person and work of the Holy Spirit. How the creeds, councils, and teachers describe them.

de-gratia.dek: What the churches have said about the grace of God and its place in salvation.

de-fide.dek: What the churches have taught about faith. Its nature and its place in salvation.

de-justificatione.dek: What the churches have taught about how sinners stand before God. The meaning of justification, and its relation to faith and works.

de-sanctificatione.dek: What the churches have taught about holiness in believers and its relation to justification.

de-ecclesia.dek: What the churches have taught about the church. Its nature, marks, and government.

de-sacramentis.dek: What the churches have taught about the sacraments or ordinances. Their number, meaning, and effect.

de-baptismo.dek: What the churches have taught about baptism. Its meaning, subjects, and mode.

de-coena.dek: What the churches have taught about the Lord's Supper or Eucharist. Its meaning and the question of Christ's presence.

de-novissimis.dek: What the churches have taught about death, judgment, and the end of all things.

de-resurrectione.dek: What the churches have said about the resurrection of the dead.
